tool_arguments.query: Arm Holdings royalty licensing revenue data center Neoverse Q3 fiscal 2025

events.content: Arm Holdings royalty licensing revenue data center Neoverse Q3 fiscal 2025

Arm Holdings’ fiscal Q3 2026 ended **December 31, 2025** and produced record revenue of **$1.242 billion**, up **26% year over year**. [[1, 2]]

- **Royalty revenue:** **$737 million**, up **27% YoY** from **$580 million** in Q3 fiscal 2025. [[2]]
- **License and other revenue:** **$505 million**, up **25% YoY** from **$403 million**. [[2]]
- Royalty revenue represented roughly **59.3%** of quarterly revenue, while license and other revenue represented roughly **40.7%**. [[2]]
- Arm attributed royalty growth to adoption of higher-royalty-rate technologies—including **Armv9** and **Arm Compute Subsystems (CSS)**—as well as rising deployment of Arm chips in data centers. [[2]]

**Data-center / Neoverse takeaways:** Arm did not disclose an absolute dollar figure for data-center or Neoverse revenue, but it stated that **data-center royalty revenue grew at a triple-digit year-over-year rate**. [[2]] Arm also said that **Neoverse CPUs surpassed one billion deployed cores** and that its share among leading hyperscalers is expected to approach **50%**. [[1]] AWS’s fifth-generation Graviton processor, based on the higher-performance **Neoverse CSS V3**, has **192 cores**, double Graviton4’s core count. [[1]] 

The central implication is that the reported $737 million of total royalties was helped by both higher Arm content/value per chip and a rapidly expanding data-center opportunity, but Arm’s Q3 disclosure does **not** separately quantify Neoverse revenue or data-center royalty dollars. [[2]]

Sources:
[S1.1] Arm delivers fourth consecutive billion-dollar revenue quarter, extending record-breaking momentum - Arm Newsroom — https://newsroom.arm.com/news/arm-q3-fye26-results
[S1.2] SEC Filing — https://investors.arm.com/node/7826/html

events.content: Arm Holdings fiscal Q2 fiscal 2026 data center Neoverse royalty revenue

Arm’s Q2 fiscal 2026, ended September 30, 2025, revenue was $1.135 billion; royalty revenue was a record $620 million, up 21% year over year, while **license and other revenue** was $515 million, up 56% year over year. [[1]] 

Royalty growth reflected higher royalty rates from Armv9 and Arm Compute Subsystems (CSS), as well as greater use of Arm-based chips in data centers. [[1]] 

For Neoverse/data center, Arm said data-center royalties doubled year over year, Neoverse had surpassed 1 billion CPUs deployed, and the Neoverse business more than doubled year over year. [[2]] 

Arm also signed one new CSS license for a data-center customer during the quarter, among three total new CSS licenses. [[3]]

tool_arguments.query: Arm Holdings fiscal Q1 fiscal 2026 data center Neoverse royalty revenue

events.content: Arm Holdings fiscal Q1 fiscal 2026 data center Neoverse royalty revenue

Arm’s Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2025; reported July 30, 2025) revenue was **$1.053 billion**, up **12% year over year** and its best first quarter to date. [[1]] [[2]]

- **Royalty revenue:** **$585 million**, up **25% YoY** from **$467 million** in Q1 FY2025. [[1]]
- **License and other revenue:** **$468 million**, down **1% YoY** from **$472 million**, which Arm attributed to normal timing and size variation in high-value license agreements and backlog contributions. [[1]]
- **License pipeline indicator:** annualized contract value was **$1.528 billion**, up **28% YoY**, while remaining performance obligations were **$2.232 billion**, up **3% YoY**. [[1]] 

Data-center demand was a stated contributor to royalty growth, alongside Armv9 adoption and the ramp of Arm Compute Subsystems (CSS); Arm did **not** disclose a dollar amount or separate growth rate for data-center royalties in its Q1 FY2026 release. [[1]] 

For **Neoverse**, Arm said it expected Arm Neoverse-based chips’ share at the top hyperscalers to reach **nearly 50% during calendar 2025**, supported by demand for high-performance, energy-efficient cloud and AI compute. [[2]] 

CSS licensing adds an important leading indicator for future royalties: Arm had signed **16 CSS licenses with 10 companies**, more than double the prior-year count; five companies were already shipping CSS-based chips, and Q1 added **three** licenses—**two data-center** and **one PC**. [[1]] 

The key read-through is that FY2026 Q1 growth was royalty-led rather than licensing-led: royalties rose $118 million year over year while licensing declined $4 million, with data-center/Neoverse deployment and higher-value Armv9/CSS content identified as principal drivers. [[1]]

Sources:
[S5.1] Document — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1973239/000197323925000023/exhibit992fye26q130-junx25.htm
[S5.2] Corrected Transcript 1-877-FACTSET www.callstreet.com Total Pages: 14 — https://investors.arm.com/static-files/57a99953-427a-4cfb-ade8-634d3564c008

tool_arguments.query: Arm Holdings fiscal Q4 fiscal 2025 full year data center Neoverse royalty revenue FY2025

events.content: Arm Holdings fiscal Q4 fiscal 2025 full year data center Neoverse royalty revenue FY2025

Arm’s fiscal 2025 ended March 31, 2025, with total revenue of **$4.007 billion**, up from **$3.233 billion** in fiscal 2024. [[1]]

- **Royalty revenue:** **$2.168 billion**, exceeding $2 billion for the first time and representing approximately **54.1%** of full-year revenue. [[2]] [[3]]
- **License and other revenue:** **$1.839 billion**, or approximately **45.9%** of total revenue. [[1]] [[3]]
- The implied year-over-year growth rates were approximately **21.8% for royalties** and **26.6% for license and other revenue**, based on FY2024 segment revenues of roughly $1.780 billion and $1.453 billion, respectively. [[1]] [[3]]

**Data-center / Neoverse read-through:** Arm did not disclose a separate full-year revenue figure specifically for data center or Neoverse in its FY2025 reporting. [[1]] [[2]] However, Arm explicitly identified increased usage of Arm-based chips in data centers as a driver of Q4 FY2025 royalty revenue, alongside Armv9 adoption and the ramp of Compute Subsystems (CSS). [[3]] In Q4, royalty revenue was **$607 million**, up **18% year over year**, while license-and-other revenue was **$634 million**, up **53% year over year**. [[3]] 

Neoverse was positioned as a key AI-data-center platform: Arm stated that the computational efficiency of its Neoverse platform was integral to AI data-center demand and noted that NVIDIA’s Armv9-based Grace Blackwell superchip had entered full production. [[2]] Arm also said FY2025 royalty growth came from all target end markets, specifically including data center, automotive, smartphones, and IoT. [[4]] 

The key analytical point is that **Neoverse/data-center exposure was an important qualitative royalty-growth driver in FY2025, but it was not separately quantified**; Arm’s reported economics remain the aggregate licensing plus per-chip royalty model. [[1]] [[3]]

Sources:

tool_arguments.query: Arm Holdings Q4 FY2026 royalty licensing revenue data center Neoverse

events.content: Arm Holdings Q4 FY2026 royalty licensing revenue data center Neoverse

Arm’s Q4 FY2026 (quarter ended March 31, 2026) revenue was a record **$1.490 billion**, up **20% year over year**. [[1]]

- **Royalty revenue:** **$671 million**, up **11% YoY** from $607 million, representing roughly **45%** of quarterly revenue. [[1]]
- **License and other revenue:** **$819 million**, up **29% YoY** from $634 million, or roughly **55%** of revenue. [[1]]
- The royalty increase reflected higher royalty rates from broader adoption of **Armv9** and **Arm Compute Subsystems (CSS)**, plus greater deployment of Arm-based chips in data centers. [[1]]
- The licensing result benefited from continued demand for Arm IP, the timing and size of several high-value licensing agreements, and backlog contributions. [[1]]

**Neoverse / data-center read-through:** management said the largest contributor to Q4 royalty growth was **cloud AI**, and that **data-center royalty revenue more than doubled YoY**. [[2]] Management specifically stated that royalties tied to chips built on **Neoverse** had doubled YoY and expected them to double again in FY2027. [[2]] Arm also introduced its **Arm AGI CPU**, its first Arm-designed chip for cloud and AI data centers, during the quarter. [[1]] 

The key investor takeaway is that Q4’s royalty growth rate of 11% understated the strategic strength in data center: the rapidly growing Neoverse/cloud-AI royalty stream was offset within the aggregate royalty line by Arm’s broader and more mature end markets, while licensing grew 29% on large-contract activity. [[2]] [[1]]

Sources:
[S10.1] UNITED STATES SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION Washington, D.C. 20549 — https://investors.arm.com/static-files/adf3bac7-1e91-442e-92e0-5f2d8f1b6a14

Neoverse was positioned as a key AI-data-center platform: Arm stated that the computational efficiency of its Neoverse platform was integral to AI data-center demand and noted that NVIDIA’s Armv9-based Grace Blackwell superchip had entered full production. [[2]] Arm also said FY2025 royalty growth came from all target end markets, specifically including data center, automotive, smartphones, and IoT. [[4]] 

The key analytical point is that **Neoverse/data-center exposure was an important qualitative royalty-growth driver in FY2025, but it was not separately quantified**; Arm’s reported economics remain the aggregate licensing plus per-chip royalty model. [[1]] [[3]]

private_messages.content:
Arm’s Q4 FY2026 (quarter ended March 31, 2026) revenue was a record **$1.490 billion**, up **20% year over year**. [[1]]

- **Royalty revenue:** **$671 million**, up **11% YoY** from $607 million, representing roughly **45%** of quarterly revenue. [[1]]
- **License and other revenue:** **$819 million**, up **29% YoY** from $634 million, or roughly **55%** of revenue. [[1]]
- The royalty increase reflected higher royalty rates from broader adoption of **Armv9** and **Arm Compute Subsystems (CSS)**, plus greater deployment of Arm-based chips in data centers. [[1]]
- The licensing result benefited from continued demand for Arm IP, the timing and size of several high-value licensing agreements, and backlog contributions. [[1]]

**Neoverse / data-center read-through:** management said the largest contributor to Q4 royalty growth was **cloud AI**, and that **data-center royalty revenue more than doubled YoY**. [[2]] Management specifically stated that royalties tied to chips built on **Neoverse** had doubled YoY and expected them to double again in FY2027. [[2]] Arm also introduced its **Arm AGI CPU**, its first Arm-designed chip for cloud and AI data centers, during the quarter. [[1]] 

The key investor takeaway is that Q4’s royalty growth rate of 11% understated the strategic strength in data center: the rapidly growing Neoverse/cloud-AI royalty stream was offset within the aggregate royalty line by Arm’s broader and more mature end markets, while licensing grew 29% on large-contract activity. [[2]] [[1]]
